record.paper_title: Two open problems in precedence constrained scheduling
record.context_brief: single-machine total tardiness with chain-like precedence and release dates
record.original_question: Determine the computational complexity of the following optimization problem. There are n jobs, all of unit processing time, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine. Each job j has an integer due date d_j and a release date r_j, so job j is unavailable before time r_j. The precedence constraints are chain-like: in the directed precedence graph on the jobs, each vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one. A feasible schedule must respect both the release dates and the precedence arcs, and if job j completes at time C_j then its tardiness is max(0, C_j - d_j). What is the complexity of finding a feasible schedule minimizing the total tardiness over all jobs?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the following single-machine scheduling problem. There are n jobs, each of unit processing time, to be processed nonpreemptively on a single machine that can handle at most one job at a time. Each job j (1 ≤ j ≤ n) has an integer due date d_j and an integer release date r_j; job j may not start before time r_j. A directed precedence graph G is given on the vertex set {1,...,n} in which every vertex has indegree at most one and outdegree at most one (so the precedence constraints form a disjoint union of chains). A feasible schedule assigns a start time S_j ≥ r_j to each job such that the intervals [S_j, S_j+1) are pairwise disjoint and S_j + 1 ≤ S_k whenever (j,k) is an arc of G. Let C_j = S_j + 1 denote the completion time of job j and let its tardiness be T_j = max(0, C_j − d_j). Determine the computational complexity of finding a feasible schedule that minimizes the total tardiness Σ_{j=1}^{n} T_j: in particular, is this problem solvable in polynomial time, or is it NP-hard?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a definitive resolution of the complexity of the unit-time single-machine total tardiness problem with chain precedence and release dates. Surveys and recent overviews of single-machine scheduling complexity (e.g., the 2024 overview on arXiv) still list related variants among unresolved cases, and no polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hardness proof for this exact problem could be confirmed. The status is therefore reported as unknown/likely still open.
